summary: Iron County lookout on Crane Mountain, surveyed in 1938 and 1956 with conflicting heights; the index marks it removed and a trail app notes foundation piers.

facts.design: four-sided steel tower with an enclosed observation cab at the top
facts.status_note: Removed. A trail app says foundation piers can be found; no agency source describes the site now.

access.note: The old tower road is listed as a trail in Mark Twain National Forest; the tower itself is gone.

visit.trail_note: Listed as a 0.9-mile trail on the old tower road, Forest Service Road 2192 (trail app)

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described a 100-foot four-sided steel tower with an enclosed top and took its survey point from the tower center
Survey recovery note gives the tower as 110 feet high with an 8-foot square house on top, which conflicts with the 1938 height

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: the 1938 survey gives 100 feet (30.5 m, the record value) and the 1956 recovery note gives 110 feet (33.5 m). The record height is left unchanged and the story gives both. Removal date is in no source; the 1970-2000 window and the piers come only from a trail app (secondary, unverified). The record point (37.4764, -90.6206) is about 20 m from the piers' coordinates in the app, so no location correction. The index names the Clark National Forest, which was set up in 1939, after the 1938 survey; the forest name is the index's label. The page carries a photo (uploads/1/5/9/1/1591048/crane-tower-missouri.jpg) with no licence stated; not added. No staffing, fire or access-status information found in any source read.
